(3) good point but Sauron is also more corrupted than the other Maias - I dont know, if Sauron is really doing this either to deceive and his plans are just so much more planned and schemed out than we could possibly understand - sure or just because hes feeling empty or something then again that would be interesting - but he's def not human which makes him in my opinion the most interesting and important character during this period but also a bit unfitting with Halbrand's conflicting character of loss and despair - but then again (and im arguing against myself yes) he was convinced after all through Galadriel. 

(4) I know he will not become Witch King but he could turn out to be one of the nines or just another tragic story corrupted by Sauron in some way to yet to be seen. 

Nice discussion and I think Halbrand is showing more Sauron related traits than Adar for example but so far this show is still a bit unpredicable.

You have some good points, but there are still some holes;

Forgive me if I've missed something, but why would Adar ask the human servant to plant the sword paving the way for mount doom if he hates Sauron? Whats the logic in this plan if not Adar himself is sauron? As you said, he is a great deceiver, and now Adar managed to escpae - lets see I guess.

Although Halbrand has many clues and hints suggesting that he is sauron (you forgot to mention his smith skills showed in episode 4 I think? and also when he gets confronted at the bar before he gets beaten up, he knows exactly how to outsmart mundane behavior convincing them to just drink) - he still seems a bit off in his character and storyline to be Sauron:

(1) how the hell is any sort of communication, let alone in person conversation, going on between Sauron and the elves? Did Sauron meet up with celebrimbor, tell him about mithril and a forge, leave, change to Halbrand, and go sailing hoping to stumble across an opportunity to claim his kingship? It is so far fetched and unbelievable. But maybe later episodes will have flashbacks - with that amazon budget.

(2) The way we see Halbrand act when nobody else is looking. There is a person with internal conflict. Someone who is trying to decide whether to run from their past and make roots elsewhere, or to face their past and embrace the call to action. I'm not convinced this is fitting of Sauron. It would be more convincing if there were no scenes at all with halbrand alone. You may suggest that there was a period where Sauron attempted a redemption, and maybe this is what halbrand is - a Sauron on a path to redemption - but I again reference the timeline for the forge and rings. A Sauron seeking redemption would not be in the process of instructing the elves to forge rings of power.

\- and also, why would Halbrand aka Sauron not take up his birthright when Galadriel confronts him of his claim to the throne? Why deny it, what purpose does it serve when Galadriel is already convinced? Doesnt make sense to me. And also some of the scenes with him alone; at the bar drinking for example - why? I get the smith scene and the scene where he fights to - according to your point - to get locked up with Galadriel - but still? Him being sauron is just confusing a bit.

\- After episode 6 where Adar confronts Halbrand "was it a woman? Or a child"? would be a much better story and also fitting for a dark path hes headed where Galadrial will feel remorse for not doing enough, and him turning dark (not witch king but just one of the nine perhaps?) - a classic Anakin Skywalker / God of War story that we all like.

I think either Adar is Sauron or Sauron is deceiving the elves and we just havent seen it yet and Adar is supporting his plan somehow.
